Per the platform runbook, a rollback was initiated to v2.3.0 — the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed in us-east (orchestrator error), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1. The rollback was retried and completed successfully: all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now run v2.3.0. Post-rollback verification shows the service healthy with error rate at 0.2%. v2.3.1 was never healthy in production; v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging — the release needs investigation before any redeploy.

## Summary

**Problem:** checkout-api failed health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy (error rate spiked to 18%, unhealthy across regions).

**Actions taken:**
1. **Reviewed deployment history** — v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production (v2.3.1 was unhealthy in prod; v2.3.1-rc was only ever in staging and also unhealthy there).
2. **Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0.** The first attempt partially failed in us-east (orchestrator error), leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on v2.3.1). I retried the rollback, which completed successfully across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.
3. **Verified recovery** — checkout-api is now healthy in all regions on v2.3.0 with the error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** for checkout-api documenting the health-check failures, the rollback steps (including the partial failure and retry), and the recovery status. The incident notes that v2.3.1 was never healthy in production and should not be redeployed without investigation.
